newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen to deploy 60,000 security forces for poll.
newsitem.headline: Yemen to deploy 60,000 security forces for poll.

text.p: Yemen will deploy 60,000 police and troops to boost security during the Arab country's parliamentary elections at the end of the month, a senior security official said on Monday.

"Some 60,000 security and army forces will not be casting their votes in the next parliamentary elections (on April 27)...This number will be responsible for protection at the elections so everything goes smoothly," said Ali Mohammad Saleh, head of the security committee for the elections.
He said the forces would not be voting because they would be on duty outside of their home constituencies.
Saleh said "the number of security forces currently on duty are estimated at 8,068, but this number will rise to 60,000 from the 22nd of this month".
Unofficial estimates put the number of Yemen's military and security forces at around 150,000.
Election officials expect about 5,000 candidates to seek votes for 301 parliamentary seats under the banners of 12 parties or as independents.
Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh last month called on the interior ministry to beef up security measures ahead of the elections.
